#     deposit  (bytes32 depositor, bytes32 recipient, bytes32 inputToken, …)   0xad5425c6  ← this
#     depositV3(address depositor, address recipient, address inputToken, …)   0x7b939232
#
#   IDENTICAL arity, IDENTICAL parameter names, IDENTICAL order. They differ only in the TYPE of
#   five parameters — the bytes32 widening that admits non-EVM addresses. `depositV3` carries no
#   deprecation annotation of any kind, and BOTH selectors are live in the deployed
#   implementation on ethereum, base AND arbitrum. So "depositV3 is the V3 function, and V3 is
#   current" is a reasonable inference and a wrong one. → FINDINGS.md F8 half B.
#
# ⚠ THE FEE IS A SUBTRACTION YOU PERFORM. There is no fee parameter. `inputAmount` is pulled from
#   you; `outputAmount` is what the recipient gets; THE DIFFERENCE IS THE RELAYER'S PAY. Set them
#   equal and the deposit SUCCEEDS, emits, locks your funds — and no relayer ever fills it,
#   because it pays nothing. Nothing reverts. See mistake #2.
#
# ⚠ THIS RECIPE COVERS THE DEPOSIT, NOT THE BRIDGE. A fork test executes the source side and
#   nothing else: the fill is a third-party relayer's action on the destination chain, settled
#   later through the HubPool. Contrast #11 cctp, which observed BOTH ends with two real
#   transfers. Stated here, in scope_notes, and in sources.json — see rejected A-REJ2.
#
